questions.q: Why does Payables Invoice Import use two separate interface tables?
options: Because headers and lines are always identical in structure
Because Oracle requires exactly two tables for every import regardless of the business object
Because one table is a backup of the other
Because an invoice has two levels — a header and one or more lines — and each maps to its own interface table
questions.explain: AP_INVOICES_INTERFACE stages header data; AP_INVOICE_LINES_INTERFACE stages line data — mirroring the invoice's own header/line structure.

questions.q: Why can't a payables invoice be successfully imported against a supplier that hasn't been loaded yet?
options: The supplier identifier on the invoice is a coded reference to an existing supplier record, which must already exist for the invoice to validate
Invoices don't actually require a supplier at all
Supplier data is irrelevant to Payables invoices
Oracle automatically creates a placeholder supplier
questions.explain: An invoice header references a supplier by its identifier. If that supplier doesn't exist, the import process has nothing valid to validate against, so the row fails.

questions.q: In the rejection scenario described, a header invoice amount is $5,000.00 but its lines sum to $4,950.00. What causes this rejection?
options: A UCM account mismatch
A macro security setting
The import process's check that line amounts sum correctly to the header's invoice amount
An invalid lookup code for currency
questions.explain: This is a header-level balancing check specific to Payables: the sum of the invoice's lines must match its header amount, or the invoice is rejected.

questions.q: Which process actually validates staged payables invoice rows and creates real, live invoices?
options: Load Interface File for Import
Import Payables Invoices
Import Journals
Generate CSV File
questions.explain: Import Payables Invoices is the product-specific import process for this module — it validates staged rows and creates real invoice records.

questions.q: Where can a consultant find the specific reason a payables invoice interface row was rejected?
options: There is no way to determine the specific reason
In the original Excel template file itself
In the ADFdi installer log
In AP_INTERFACE_REJECTIONS, which records exactly which row failed and why
questions.explain: AP_INTERFACE_REJECTIONS is the dedicated structure that stores rejection detail for rows that failed Payables invoice import, consistent with the interface-table-review technique from Chapter 3.
